lesson_title: Four Boxes That Saved Our Stall From the Rain
hook_text: It rained on our market day. We sold out anyway, because of four little boxes.
clip_script: Four boxes: S, W, O, T. Strengths, inside and good: Gogo's vetkoek recipe, cheap flour. Weaknesses, inside and bad: one pot, no experience. Opportunities, outside and good: a cold July day and nobody else selling hot food. Threats, outside and bad: a chips stall, rising oil prices, rain. Then, actions. Put Gogo on the poster. Borrow a second pot. Set up by the gate. Buy oil early and ask where we can fry if it rains. Market day: it rains. We fry under the walkway. Sold out by second break. That is a SWOT analysis.
visual_style: A whiteboard grid of four boxes filling with icons, then arrows turning each box into an action, ending with rain and a sold-out sign.
mood: Clever and satisfying, planning pays off.
pacing: Quick box-by-box fill, then fast actions and a rainy-day payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a SWOT grid for your own Entrepreneur's Day idea.
